notes: All four runs used newly owned private-Xvfb Rhino sessions and documented public APIs. No existing user window or proprietary implementation was inspected.

Retained observations concatenate all 48 competition results, all 24 order repetitions and all 12 final picking diagnostic results. The preliminary 12 line-only diagnostics repeat the same picking inputs and are hashed separately, not counted as additional retained cases.
Per-wire mathematical agreement uses the observed component only to identify the wire being tested; it is not a claim that native wire selection matches Rhino.
All 24 changed-sequence order repetitions reproduce the point and component. Raw vertex order can change selection without changing the boundary, camera or click.

Public ordinary picking and actual Near snapping select different edges in retained counterexamples. No first-edge, minimum-distance or ordinary-picking heuristic was substituted into native mesh snapping.

The native projected_object_snap diagnostic consumes only sources, camera/click and policy. Its Python replay leaves parity mismatches as failures, with no target-dependent inputs or widened epsilon. None compares non-admission only; these probes do not test history or establish speed parity.
